video.title: How to Buy Big Things with Little Money

summary: Chris Koerner explains ways to acquire property, businesses, and other valuable assets with little upfront cash, drawing on his own purchases and negotiations. He focuses on seller financing structures, building trust with sellers, staying flexible about the asset, and documenting a project publicly to attract customers or investors. His examples include real estate, short-term rentals, RV parks, and a landscaping business. The main takeaway is to reduce risk for the seller, negotiate terms creatively, and be ready to walk away if the deal does not work on the numbers.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; shares personal acquisition experience and examples.

ideas.name: Buy businesses and assets with little cash using creative financing
ideas.one_liner: Acquire a business or asset by negotiating seller financing, flexible terms, and a relationship of trust.
ideas.business_model: Acquire an existing business or asset, improve or operate it, then earn from its cash flow or resale.
ideas.customer: Sellers of businesses, real estate, or other assets; the buyer is the founder or operator.
ideas.problem: The buyer wants an asset but lacks the cash for a conventional down payment or financing terms.
ideas.offer: A purchase proposal that adjusts the down payment, timing, payment schedule, collateral, or future profit share to suit both parties.

pricing.model: Negotiated purchase price and financing terms.
pricing.notes: Terms depend on the asset and seller. The transcript gives several hypothetical structures rather than one standard price.

acquisition_channels.details: Find owners in an asset class, build a relationship, visit in person more than once, follow up, and explain how the buyer can add value.

quote.text: Visit him in person multiple times, follow up with him, bring your spouse and kids if that's the case.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Document the project on free social platforms to build an audience and attract prospective customers or investors.

quote.text: If you bring the world along with you through these free media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, Tik Tok, whatever, then you can skip the line.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: The buyer operates or improves the acquired asset. The seller may receive installments, interest, a balloon payment, future appreciation, or another negotiated form of consideration.
unit_economics_claims: Chris says he bought an $800,000 business with $50,000 down.
The transcript gives hypothetical buy-and-resell math for a landscaping business.
tools: ChatGPT for generating alternative financing structures
Banks for conventional or alternative loan options
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated; the purpose is to reduce the amount of cash required upfront.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated; depends on the asset and financing terms.

acquisition.how: Finding and persuading an owner depends on trust and often repeated personal contact; software can assist with research but cannot replace the relationship.

onboarding.how: Document collection and deal administration can use software, but parties and advisers must agree and review the contract.

delivery.how: Operating a purchased business or physical asset requires human oversight and may involve physical work.

billing.how: Scheduled payments can be automated, but payment terms and servicing need human setup and monitoring.

support.how: Seller relations and operational issues require human judgement and communication.

uk_applicability.notes: Seller financing and negotiated purchase terms can work in the UK, but legal, tax, lending, and property rules differ and need local advice.

risks: A balloon payment may become due before the buyer can refinance or sell; default can return the asset to the seller.
A seller with a second lien position may recover little or nothing if a senior lender is paid first.
Interest-only payments do not reduce principal and interest may compound.
A lease-to-own or master lease can leave the buyer with operating risk and no ownership if the option is not exercised.
Borrowing from friends and family can damage valuable personal relationships.
Do not become emotionally attached to a deal; be willing to walk away.

quotes.text: your best shot of being able to buy something big with little money is seller financing, preferably as close to 100% as possible.

quotes.text: You've got to be willing to build a relationship of trust.

tactics.name: Document the project publicly
steps: Start a social account before launch, even with no followers.
Use a phone and informal videos to show planning, building, and fundraising.
Study other creators in the niche: hooks, music, posting frequency, asset type, and comments.
Paste comment text into ChatGPT to identify themes that may resonate with viewers.
Optimize for shares, comments, and average view duration, not likes alone.
Repeat the formats that work and try to improve each video.

quote.text: What are their hooks? What background music are they using? How often are they posting? What days are they posting?
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Broaden the asset search and build seller trust
steps: Choose an asset class, then stay flexible on geography, price point, size, and type within it.
Look for an owner who is willing to get to know you and whom you also like.
Learn about the owner's asset class and acknowledge what they know.
Offer value, compliment the property sincerely, visit more than once, and follow up.
Share relevant personal context and common ground to make the relationship more familiar.

quote.text: You've got to be willing to build a relationship of trust.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Ask for alternative bank loan options
steps: If a bank presents a costly loan condition such as PMI, ask what other options exist.
Explain that the proposed cost makes the deal unaffordable.
Keep speaking with banks until one offers terms that work.

quote.text: I read that I don't have to pay that. and they were like, "Uh, all right. I don't think it's going to work, but let me see if there are other options."
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Frame seller financing around the seller's benefits
steps: Present the tangible benefits of the proposed terms to the seller.
Explain the buyer's story and relevant industry experience.
Use a specific plan for improving the asset and show how the seller can be protected.
Consider an ongoing profit share if the seller believes the asset has untapped potential.

quote.text: You've got to frame it in a way that really highlights the positives for them. Both the tangibles and the intangibles.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a balloon payment to defer principal
steps: Negotiate a small initial payment and manageable monthly payments.
Set a balloon due date in the contract.
Plan to refinance or sell the asset before the balloon is due.
Check the default and lien terms before signing.

quote.text: The idea with this structure is to either refinance or sell the asset before then.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Offer graduated payments to build seller confidence
steps: Start with payments the new business can afford.
Increase payments on a schedule as the buyer establishes a track record.
Use the schedule to show the seller that payments begin immediately and the buyer is acting in good faith.

quote.text: suggest graduated payments because they can almost have the same purpose, which is to save you money in your payments upfront
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Combine bank debt with a seller carryback
steps: Calculate the down payment required by the bank and the buyer's available cash.
Ask the seller to carry the funding gap as a note.
Discuss the seller's junior lien position and the risk of being behind the bank.
Consider bringing in friends or family for part of the buyer contribution only after weighing relationship risk.

quote.text: A partial seller carryback would be for the seller to put 150 grand on the line
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Trade future appreciation for better terms
steps: If the seller believes the asset can be worth more after improvements, ask them to improve the current financing terms.
Offer a defined share of future rents or profits tied to specific milestones.
Write the valuation triggers and payment share into the agreement.

quote.text: How about you give me better terms on the seller financing and then I cut you into those future profits.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Use a master lease with an option to buy
steps: Lease the property while the seller keeps title.
Set a monthly payment and a predetermined purchase price and date.
Define the right to walk away and what happens to the property if the buyer does not exercise the option.
Use time under the lease to test whether the improvement plan works.

quote.text: It's a master lease agreement with the option to purchase at a predetermined price at a certain predetermined time in the future.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Swap price, rate, down payment, services, or collateral
steps: Offer a higher interest rate or purchase price in exchange for less cash down.
Consider consulting or marketing services in place of a cash down payment.
Consider offering collateral only after reviewing what default would mean.
Use ChatGPT to generate alternative term combinations, then review them with appropriate advisers.

quote.text: How about 8% interest and 0% down?

tactics.name: Consider subject-to or delayed down payment terms
steps: For a subject-to structure, discuss taking over payments while the existing loan remains in the seller's name.
For a delayed down payment, propose a future payment date and define what happens if it is not paid.
Review the existing loan and contract terms carefully before proceeding.

quote.text: The debt stays in the seller's name and you come out of pocket little to nothing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Stay willing to walk away
steps: Evaluate the deal on its numbers and risks.
Do not treat one asset or seller as the only opportunity.
Walk away if the financing, operations, or downside protection do not work.

quote.text: You've got to be willing to walk from any deal at any time. It should only be math to you.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner
